notes.meaning: Jotham became king of Judah when he was twenty-five years old, and he ruled in Jerusalem for sixteen years. His mother Jerushah was the daughter of Zadok, which linked him to a respected priestly family. He had already spent years running the government while his father Uzziah lived apart due to leprosy.

Jotham followed the good patterns of his father Uzziah by obeying the Lord. He also learned from his father's downfall and refused to force his way into the temple to act like a priest. Even though the king was faithful, the people of the land still continued in their corrupt and idol-worshiping practices.

Jotham began his construction projects at the temple of the Lord, repairing and beautifying the northern Upper Gate. He also carried out extensive repairs on the wall of Ophel, a hill that connected the palace area to the temple mount. By putting God's house first, he showed that worship was the true center of his kingdom.

The king expanded his building work into the countryside to protect his people. He set up towns in the mountainous regions and built forts and watchtowers in the thick forests. These defenses helped guard farmers and shepherds against sudden attacks by raiders.

When the Ammonites rebelled against Judah, Jotham led his army into battle and crushed them. He made them pay a large tribute of silver along with huge quantities of wheat and barley each year. The Ammonites continued paying this heavy tax for three years before the payments stopped.

Jotham became strong and successful because he deliberately aligned his daily life with the Lord his God. He did not waver like earlier kings, but stayed steady in keeping God's commands. True strength in life comes from walking faithfully with God step by step.

Other details about Jotham's military victories and public deeds were recorded in the official royal histories of Israel and Judah. These writings included the early skirmishes against Syria and Israel that began near the close of his days. His reign was remembered as an honorable and stable period in the nation's past.

The text repeats Jotham's starting age of twenty-five and his sixteen-year reign to give a final summary of his life. He died at forty-one years old, right in the prime of his manhood. Unlike his predecessors, he never ruined his good name by turning away from God in his old age.

When Jotham died, he received an honorable burial alongside his royal ancestors in the City of David. His son Ahaz took over the throne after him. Tragically, Ahaz turned out to be an ungodly ruler who refused to walk in his father's righteous footsteps.
